title: A Chatbot-Free Childhood Will Be a Status Symbol
excerpt: AI is like ultra-processed food for developing brains.
content_html:
The human brain has evolved to learn from specific instructors. When a child hears a gentle spoken word or a soothing lullaby from another person, when their cry is responded to, their brain lights up. Nurturing interactions, or what child-development experts call “serve and return” exchanges, help shape and strengthen the 1 million new neural connections taking place in a child’s brain every single second. Every time a child cries or serves up a bid for attention and receives a caregiver’s response, that back-and-forth helps build the circuits underlying their communication, learning, and emotional well-being. No other input, not even Johann Pachelbel’s Canon in D performed by the Berlin Philharmonic, is capable of activating the neural circuitry the way human interaction does.

Until now. Generative AI may be the first technology in history sophisticated enough to mimic the social interactions that build our brains. Research has demonstrated that infants as young as six months old respond physiologically to interactions with humanoid robots in ways that mirror their response to live humans; another, small-scale experimental study recently found that, after young children interacted with a chatbot, most of them for the first time, they asserted that the AI could perceive the world with humanlike senses and understand and learn as people do.

This technology is already showing up in children’s lives. The talking plush robot that purports to be a child’s best friend is obviously driven by AI, but many parents may not realize that their Amazon Echo recently received a software update that converts the Alexa voice assistant into a full-blown chatbot, using the same fundamental tech that fuels ChatGPT; toddlers asking for information about animals or a joke or a bedtime story may quickly find themselves in the habit of engaging socially with a large language model.

As a pediatric surgeon, researcher, and technologist who has spent decades studying how children’s brains develop, I am concerned about these technologies rolling out and being used by children in the home and at school before we have a full sense of their safety and what they do to young minds. And I am compelled to point out what we do know about human development: that human connection, in all of its imperfection, is foundational to brain development. It can’t be engineered or recovered later.

When a disruption as significant as the AI revolution occurs, people might look for a comparison to make sense of the transformation. In this case, many people instinctively think of social media. After all, it, too, amounted to a large-scale technological experiment that produced unexpected problems that we are still attempting to fully comprehend. But even that comparison is insufficient, because interactive AI—and its ability to mimic the serve-and-return exchanges that wire developing brains—is utterly, fundamentally different from every consumer technology that came before it.

During the most foundational period of brain development, social interaction of the sort that AI can now emulate isn’t entertainment for the developing brain. It’s nutrition. Once you see it that way, the right parallel snaps into focus. A more apt comparison than social media is food—more precisely, processed food.

Read: Coke, Twinkies, Skittles, and … whole-grain bread?

For a long time, no one needed to specify that food was farm-raised. The alternative didn’t exist. Food was grown on farms and in gardens and was prepared in homes and in kitchens. But in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, that changed. Food production was industrialized, transformed by genuinely beneficial innovations such as canning, refrigeration, preservation, and mass distribution. Real and urgent problems were addressed: Growing cities were fed, harsh winters became less lethal, life expectancy increased, and kids grew taller and lived longer.

But in the early days, food manufacturers were conducting their own uncontrolled experiments. Preservatives and additives flooded the food supply as companies adopted solutions that they promised were safe: morphine in cough syrup, chalk in milk, formaldehyde in meat. A government chemist, Harvey Washington Wiley, recognized that these evidence-free innovations posed a threat to public health. To prove this, Wiley recruited a cadre of young men willing to eat meals laced with those very preservatives while scientists observed the effects. The suffering of this so-called Poison Squad helped spark the Pure Food and Drug Act of 1906.

From the February 1909 issue: The food of the city worker

We’re in a modern Wiley moment. Innovations in artificial intelligence are delivering very real benefits to today’s families: diagnostic aids that catch developmental delays earlier than human screeners likely can, real-time translation tools that allow non-English-speaking immigrant parents to engage with their children’s teachers, productivity apps that reduce the administrative burdens weighing down many parents and educators. But these innovations have also unleashed obvious dangers: teddy bears that describe sexual kinks or teach toddlers to light matches, AI-generated videos that highlight made-up letters and words.

Despite these dramatic examples of AI gone wrong, the real danger—as demonstrated by our food supply—is what happens when these systems work exactly as designed.

By the mid-20th century, food companies had discovered something more profitable than feeding people: engineering the desire to keep eating. They hired scientists—chemists, flavor engineers, behavioral researchers—to find the precise formulas that would override the body’s natural signal that said “enough.” They discovered the “bliss point”—the precise combination of sugar, fat, and salt that maximizes pleasure in the human brain—and engineered foods to hit this target. They began producing what is now often called ultra-processed food.

This new food looked like its more natural predecessors. It came in familiar shapes. It sat on the same shelves. But something fundamental had changed. Although some ambiguities and controversies surround what foods fall into the broad term ultra-processed—in some respects, it’s a fancy way of saying “junk food”—many of these items are filled with additives and are engineered to be easy to eat and digest in large quantities. They may use hyper-palatable combinations that have been engineered to light up our brain’s reward systems. How could natural foods compete with that?

In short: They couldn’t. Whole foods slowly disappeared from our diet. Today, the average American receives 55 percent of their daily calories from ultra-processed foods—items that didn’t even exist a century ago. For children ages 1 to 18, the number is close to 62 percent. The amount of calories that adults consumed from whole foods decreased from 32.7 to 27.4 percent from 2001 to 2018, according to the CDC’s National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. According to a 2021 CDC analysis, nearly a third of American children ages 1 to 5 didn’t eat fruit daily, and nearly half didn’t eat vegetables daily. More than half drank sugar-sweetened beverages weekly.

Food companies developed truly remarkable innovations to solve very real challenges. But with those innovations in hand, they also set out to grow revenue. The same market logic is now being applied to our interaction with tech. The underlying capabilities of AI are remarkable, but they can also be formulated to optimize for engagement.

At a glance, a child talking to an AI companion looks like a child participating in conversation. But essential, quiet interactions have been stripped away. Imperfections, delays, and the need to apologize or rephrase something may seem like flaws in human communication, but they are, in fact, crucial developmental building blocks. The small cycle of rupture and repair that occurs following a misunderstanding, played out thousands of times over a childhood, is how resilience, flexibility, and emotional regulation get built. It’s how children develop the most important relational skills: trusting that relationships can survive conflict, and staying connected with others through discomfort.

From the December 2025 issue: The age of anti-social media is here

Remove the friction from childhood, and the social-emotional system never gets what it needs to properly develop. The neural architecture that was supposed to be built through imperfect, sometimes-frustrating human interaction may never fully form. Neither may frustration tolerance, empathy, or resilience. Cognitive skills may suffer too. Developmental scientists have long understood that children learn and grow by encountering tasks just beyond their current ability. This is called the “zone of proximal development,” and AI systems designed to meet a child exactly where they are risk denying them the opportunity to ever reach that zone.

Because AI companions have been engineered to remove every imperfection—the misunderstanding, the delay, the repair—a child’s social-emotional system never has to work. Ultra-processed foods stripped the fiber from diets, and engagement-optimized AI might strip the friction from childhood. The developing mind, like the gut, needs resistance to grow. Friction isn’t an obstacle to development; it is development.

Not everyone will be equally affected by the rollout of this new technology. People who have very low food security consume roughly 3 percent more ultra-processed food than those who have high food security do, in part because the cost for each calorie of unprocessed foods is more than 2.5 times that of ultra-processed foods. However, high-income families began pivoting away from ultra-processed foods as soon as the potential harms of such foods became apparent. “Clean” ingredients, minimally processed foods, and organic produce became available—and affordable—to those with resources. An “organic” diet became a status symbol.

Read: The best parenting hack is being rich

An identical pattern is emerging with AI. Many of the engineers and executives building these products are going screen-free at home and doubling down on unstructured play. Jack Clark, a co-founder of Anthropic, told Ezra Klein earlier this year that the idea of his young daughter having “unfettered” access to the YouTube algorithm “freaks me out.” He added, “I have the classic Californian-technology-executive view of not having that much technology around for children.”

If the food parallel holds, then engagement-optimized AI will become the new Dollar Menu, concentrating in the lives of the children who can least afford its developmental cost. The Pew Research Center has already demonstrated through survey data that teens in lower-income households are more likely than those from higher-income homes to rely on chatbots for homework help.

We don’t yet have a large-scale study of children raised on ultra-processed interaction. That research is still decades away. But what keeps me up at night is the possibility that we’ll allow human connection to become the new organic—cherished and protected by the wealthy, and out of reach for everyone else.

This article has been adapted from Dana Suskind’s new book, Human Raised: Nurturing Connection, Curiosity & Lifelong Learning in the Age of AI.

By

Dana Suskind

sentences.en: Food production was industrialized, transformed by genuinely beneficial innovations such as canning, refrigeration, preservation, and mass distribution.
sentences.zh: 食品生产实现了工业化，并通过罐头、冷藏、保存和大规模分销等真正有益的创新实现了转变。

sentences.en: Real and urgent problems were addressed: Growing cities were fed, harsh winters became less lethal, life expectancy increased, and kids grew taller and lived longer.
sentences.zh: 现实而紧迫的问题得到了解决：不断发展的城市得到了食物，严酷的冬天变得不那么致命，预期寿命增加，孩子们长得更高、寿命更长。

blocks.html_en: But in the early days, food manufacturers were conducting their own uncontrolled experiments. Preservatives and additives flooded the food supply as companies adopted solutions that they promised were safe: morphine in cough syrup, chalk in milk, formaldehyde in meat. A government chemist, Harvey Washington Wiley, recognized that these evidence-free innovations posed a threat to public health. To prove this, Wiley recruited a cadre of young men willing to eat meals laced with those very preservatives while scientists observed the effects. The suffering of this so-called Poison Squad helped spark the Pure Food and Drug Act of 1906.

sentences.en: But in the early days, food manufacturers were conducting their own uncontrolled experiments.
sentences.zh: 但在早期，食品制造商自己进行不受控制的实验。

sentences.en: Preservatives and additives flooded the food supply as companies adopted solutions that they promised were safe: morphine in cough syrup, chalk in milk, formaldehyde in meat.
sentences.zh: 随着公司采用他们承诺安全的解决方案，防腐剂和添加剂充斥着食品供应：止咳糖浆中的吗啡、牛奶中的白垩、肉类中的甲醛。

sentences.en: A government chemist, Harvey Washington Wiley, recognized that these evidence-free innovations posed a threat to public health.
sentences.zh: 政府化学家哈维·华盛顿·威利（Harvey Washington Wiley）认识到这些未经证实的创新对公共健康构成了威胁。

sentences.en: To prove this, Wiley recruited a cadre of young men willing to eat meals laced with those very preservatives while scientists observed the effects.
sentences.zh: 为了证明这一点，威利招募了一批年轻人，他们愿意吃含有这些防腐剂的食物，同时科学家观察其影响。

sentences.en: The suffering of this so-called Poison Squad helped spark the Pure Food and Drug Act of 1906.
sentences.zh: 这支所谓的“毒药小队”的苦难促成了 1906 年《纯净食品和药品法案》的出台。

blocks.html_en: We’re in a modern Wiley moment. Innovations in artificial intelligence are delivering very real benefits to today’s families: diagnostic aids that catch developmental delays earlier than human screeners likely can, real-time translation tools that allow non-English-speaking immigrant parents to engage with their children’s teachers, productivity apps that reduce the administrative burdens weighing down many parents and educators. But these innovations have also unleashed obvious dangers: teddy bears that describe sexual kinks or teach toddlers to light matches, AI-generated videos that highlight made-up letters and words.

sentences.en: We’re in a modern Wiley moment.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于现代 Wiley 时刻。

sentences.en: Innovations in artificial intelligence are delivering very real benefits to today’s families: diagnostic aids that catch developmental delays earlier than human screeners likely can, real-time translation tools that allow non-English-speaking immigrant parents to engage with their children’s teachers, productivity apps that reduce the administrative burdens weighing down many parents and educators.
sentences.zh: 人工智能的创新正在为当今的家庭带来非常实实在在的好处：比人类筛查人员更早发现发育迟缓的诊断辅助工具、允许非英语移民父母与孩子的老师互动的实时翻译工具、减轻许多父母和教育工作者的行政负担的生产力应用程序。

sentences.en: But these innovations have also unleashed obvious dangers: teddy bears that describe sexual kinks or teach toddlers to light matches, AI-generated videos that highlight made-up letters and words.
sentences.zh: 但这些创新也带来了明显的危险：泰迪熊会描述性怪癖或教幼儿点燃火柴，人工智能生成的视频会突出显示虚构的字母和单词。

blocks.html_en: Despite these dramatic examples of AI gone wrong, the real danger—as demonstrated by our food supply—is what happens when these systems work exactly as designed.

sentences.en: Despite these dramatic examples of AI gone wrong, the real danger—as demonstrated by our food supply—is what happens when these systems work exactly as designed.
sentences.zh: 尽管存在这些人工智能出错的戏剧性例子，但真正的危险（正如我们的食物供应所证明的那样）是当这些系统完全按照设计运行时会发生什么。

blocks.html_en: By the mid-20th century, food companies had discovered something more profitable than feeding people: engineering the desire to keep eating. They hired scientists—chemists, flavor engineers, behavioral researchers—to find the precise formulas that would override the body’s natural signal that said “enough.” They discovered the “bliss point”—the precise combination of sugar, fat, and salt that maximizes pleasure in the human brain—and engineered foods to hit this target. They began producing what is now often called ultra-processed food.

sentences.en: By the mid-20th century, food companies had discovered something more profitable than feeding people: engineering the desire to keep eating.
sentences.zh: 到了 20 世纪中叶，食品公司发现了比养活人们更有利可图的东西：激发人们继续吃东西的欲望。

sentences.en: They hired scientists—chemists, flavor engineers, behavioral researchers—to find the precise formulas that would override the body’s natural signal that said “enough.”
sentences.zh: 他们聘请了科学家——化学家、风味工程师、行为研究人员——来寻找精确的配方，以超越身体发出的“够了”的自然信号。

sentences.en: They discovered the “bliss point”—the precise combination of sugar, fat, and salt that maximizes pleasure in the human brain—and engineered foods to hit this target.
sentences.zh: 他们发现了“幸福点”——糖、脂肪和盐的精确组合，可以最大限度地提高人脑的愉悦感——并设计了食物来达到这一目标。

sentences.en: They began producing what is now often called ultra-processed food.
sentences.zh: 他们开始生产现在所谓的超加工食品。

blocks.html_en: This new food looked like its more natural predecessors. It came in familiar shapes. It sat on the same shelves. But something fundamental had changed. Although some ambiguities and controversies surround what foods fall into the broad term ultra-processed—in some respects, it’s a fancy way of saying “junk food”—many of these items are filled with additives and are engineered to be easy to eat and digest in large quantities. They may use hyper-palatable combinations that have been engineered to light up our brain’s reward systems. How could natural foods compete with that?

sentences.en: This new food looked like its more natural predecessors.
sentences.zh: 这种新食物看起来就像它更天然的前身。

sentences.en: It came in familiar shapes.
sentences.zh: 它以熟悉的形状出现。

sentences.en: It sat on the same shelves.
sentences.zh: 它位于同一个架子上。

sentences.en: But something fundamental had changed.
sentences.zh: 但一些根本性的事情发生了变化。

sentences.en: Although some ambiguities and controversies surround what foods fall into the broad term ultra-processed—in some respects, it’s a fancy way of saying “junk food”—many of these items are filled with additives and are engineered to be easy to eat and digest in large quantities.
sentences.zh: 尽管对于哪些食品属于广义的超加工食品存在一些模糊性和争议——在某些方面，这是“垃圾食品”的一种奇特说法——但其中许多食品都含有添加剂，并且经过精心设计，易于大量食用和消化。

sentences.en: They may use hyper-palatable combinations that have been engineered to light up our brain’s reward systems.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会使用经过精心设计的超美味组合来点亮我们大脑的奖励系统。

sentences.en: How could natural foods compete with that?
sentences.zh: 天然食品如何与之竞争？

blocks.html_en: In short: They couldn’t. Whole foods slowly disappeared from our diet. Today, the average American receives 55 percent of their daily calories from ultra-processed foods—items that didn’t even exist a century ago. For children ages 1 to 18, the number is close to 62 percent. The amount of calories that adults consumed from whole foods decreased from 32.7 to 27.4 percent from 2001 to 2018, according to the CDC’s National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. According to a 2021 CDC analysis, nearly a third of American children ages 1 to 5 didn’t eat fruit daily, and nearly half didn’t eat vegetables daily. More than half drank sugar-sweetened beverages weekly.

sentences.en: In short: They couldn’t.
sentences.zh: 简而言之：他们不能。

sentences.en: Whole foods slowly disappeared from our diet.
sentences.zh: 全食慢慢从我们的饮食中消失。

sentences.en: Today, the average American receives 55 percent of their daily calories from ultra-processed foods—items that didn’t even exist a century ago.
sentences.zh: 如今，美国人平均每天摄入的热量有 55% 来自超加工食品，而这些食品在一个世纪前甚至还不存在。

sentences.en: For children ages 1 to 18, the number is close to 62 percent.
sentences.zh: 对于 1 至 18 岁的儿童，这一数字接近 62%。

sentences.zh: 根据 2021 年 CDC 的分析，近三分之一的 1 至 5 岁美国儿童每天不吃水果，近一半的儿童每天不吃蔬菜。

sentences.en: More than half drank sugar-sweetened beverages weekly.
sentences.zh: 超过一半的人每周喝含糖饮料。

blocks.html_en: Food companies developed truly remarkable innovations to solve very real challenges. But with those innovations in hand, they also set out to grow revenue. The same market logic is now being applied to our interaction with tech. The underlying capabilities of AI are remarkable, but they can also be formulated to optimize for engagement.

sentences.en: Food companies developed truly remarkable innovations to solve very real challenges.
sentences.zh: 食品公司开发出真正卓越的创新来解决非常现实的挑战。

sentences.en: But with those innovations in hand, they also set out to grow revenue.
sentences.zh: 但有了这些创新，他们也开始增加收入。

sentences.en: The same market logic is now being applied to our interaction with tech.
sentences.zh: 同样的市场逻辑现在也被应用到我们与科技的互动中。

sentences.en: The underlying capabilities of AI are remarkable, but they can also be formulated to optimize for engagement.
sentences.zh: 人工智能的基本功能非常出色，但也可以对其进行优化以提高参与度。

blocks.html_en: At a glance, a child talking to an AI companion looks like a child participating in conversation. But essential, quiet interactions have been stripped away. Imperfections, delays, and the need to apologize or rephrase something may seem like flaws in human communication, but they are, in fact, crucial developmental building blocks. The small cycle of rupture and repair that occurs following a misunderstanding, played out thousands of times over a childhood, is how resilience, flexibility, and emotional regulation get built. It’s how children develop the most important relational skills: trusting that relationships can survive conflict, and staying connected with others through discomfort.

sentences.zh: 但重要的、安静的互动已被剥夺。

sentences.zh: 不完美、拖延以及道歉或改写某些事情的需要似乎是人类沟通中的缺陷，但事实上，它们是至关重要的发展基石。

sentences.zh: 误解之后发生的破裂和修复的小循环在童年时期上演了数千次，这就是韧性、灵活性和情绪调节能力的建立过程。

blocks.html_en: Remove the friction from childhood, and the social-emotional system never gets what it needs to properly develop. The neural architecture that was supposed to be built through imperfect, sometimes-frustrating human interaction may never fully form. Neither may frustration tolerance, empathy, or resilience. Cognitive skills may suffer too. Developmental scientists have long understood that children learn and grow by encountering tasks just beyond their current ability. This is called the “zone of proximal development,” and AI systems designed to meet a child exactly where they are risk denying them the opportunity to ever reach that zone.

sentences.en: Remove the friction from childhood, and the social-emotional system never gets what it needs to properly develop.
sentences.zh: 如果消除童年时期的摩擦，社交情感系统就永远得不到正常发展所需的东西。

sentences.en: The neural architecture that was supposed to be built through imperfect, sometimes-frustrating human interaction may never fully form.
sentences.zh: 本应通过不完美、有时令人沮丧的人类互动构建的神经结构可能永远不会完全形成。

sentences.en: Neither may frustration tolerance, empathy, or resilience.
sentences.zh: 挫折容忍度、同理心或复原力也不会。

sentences.en: Cognitive skills may suffer too.
sentences.zh: 认知技能也可能受到影响。

sentences.en: Developmental scientists have long understood that children learn and grow by encountering tasks just beyond their current ability.
sentences.zh: 发展科学家很早就认识到，孩子们通过遇到超出其当前能力的任务来学习和成长。

sentences.en: This is called the “zone of proximal development,” and AI systems designed to meet a child exactly where they are risk denying them the opportunity to ever reach that zone.
sentences.zh: 这被称为“最近发展区”，人工智能系统旨在准确地满足孩子所处的风险，从而剥夺他们到达该区域的机会。

blocks.html_en: Because AI companions have been engineered to remove every imperfection—the misunderstanding, the delay, the repair—a child’s social-emotional system never has to work. Ultra-processed foods stripped the fiber from diets, and engagement-optimized AI might strip the friction from childhood. The developing mind, like the gut, needs resistance to grow. Friction isn’t an obstacle to development; it is development.

blocks.html_en: Not everyone will be equally affected by the rollout of this new technology. People who have very low food security consume roughly 3 percent more ultra-processed food than those who have high food security do, in part because the cost for each calorie of unprocessed foods is more than 2.5 times that of ultra-processed foods. However, high-income families began pivoting away from ultra-processed foods as soon as the potential harms of such foods became apparent. “Clean” ingredients, minimally processed foods, and organic produce became available—and affordable—to those with resources. An “organic” diet became a status symbol.

blocks.html_en: An identical pattern is emerging with AI. Many of the engineers and executives building these products are going screen-free at home and doubling down on unstructured play. Jack Clark, a co-founder of Anthropic, told Ezra Klein earlier this year that the idea of his young daughter having “unfettered” access to the YouTube algorithm “freaks me out.” He added, “I have the classic Californian-technology-executive view of not having that much technology around for children.”

But what keeps me up at night is the possibility that we’ll allow human connection to become the new organic—cherished and protected by the wealthy, and out of reach for everyone else.

content_html_zh:
人类的大脑已经进化到可以向特定的导师学习。 当孩子听到别人轻柔的话语或舒缓的摇篮曲时，当他们的哭声得到回应时，他们的大脑就会亮起来。 培育性互动，或者儿童发展专家所说的“服务与回报”交流，有助于塑造和加强儿童大脑中每秒发生的 100 万个新神经连接。 每当孩子哭泣或寻求关注并得到照顾者的回应时，这种来回帮助建立他们的沟通、学习和情感健康的回路。 没有其他输入能够像人类互动那样激活神经回路，甚至连柏林爱乐乐团演奏的约翰·帕赫贝尔的 D 大调卡农也无法做到。

到目前为止。 生成式人工智能可能是历史上第一个足够复杂的技术，可以模仿构建我们大脑的社交互动。 研究表明，六个月大的婴儿对与人形机器人的互动的生理反应与他们对活人的反应相似。最近的另一项小规模实验研究发现，在幼儿与聊天机器人（其中大多数是第一次）互动后，他们断言人工智能可以用类似人类的感官感知世界，并像人类一样理解和学习。

这项技术已经出现在孩子们的生活中。 这个会说话的毛绒机器人自称是孩子最好的朋友，显然是由人工智能驱动的，但许多父母可能没有意识到他们的 Amazon Echo 最近收到了软件更新，将 Alexa 语音助手转换为成熟的聊天机器人，使用与 ChatGPT 相同的基本技术；幼儿询问有关动物、笑话或睡前故事的信息可能很快就会发现自己养成了与大型语言模型进行社交互动的习惯。

作为一名花费数十年时间研究儿童大脑如何发育的儿科外科医生、研究员和技术专家，我担心这些技术在我们充分了解这些技术的安全性以及它们对年轻人的影响之前，在家庭和学校中被儿童使用和使用。 我不得不指出我们对人类发展的了解：人类的联系尽管不完美，但却是大脑发展的基础。 以后无法对其进行设计或恢复。

当像人工智能革命这样重大的颠覆发生时，人们可能会通过比较来理解这种转变。 说到这里，很多人本能地想到了社交媒体。 毕竟，这也相当于一次大规模的技术实验，产生了我们仍在试图完全理解的意想不到的问题。 但即使这样的比较也是不够的，因为交互式人工智能——以及它模仿连接发育中的大脑的发球和回球交换的能力——与之前的每一种消费技术完全、根本不同。

在大脑发育的最基本时期，人工智能现在可以模拟的社交互动对于发育中的大脑来说并不是娱乐。 这是营养。 一旦你这样看，正确的平行线就会成为焦点。 比社交媒体更贴切的比喻是食品——更准确地说，是加工食品。

阅读：可乐、奶油夹心饼干、彩虹糖和…… 全麦面包？

很长一段时间以来，没有人需要明确指出食物是农场饲养的。 替代方案并不存在。 食物是在农场和花园里种植的，是在家庭和厨房里准备的。 但在 19 世纪末和 20 世纪初，情况发生了变化。 食品生产实现了工业化，并通过罐头、冷藏、保存和大规模分销等真正有益的创新实现了转变。 现实而紧迫的问题得到了解决：不断发展的城市得到了食物，严酷的冬天变得不那么致命，预期寿命增加，孩子们长得更高、寿命更长。

但在早期，食品制造商自己进行不受控制的实验。 随着公司采用他们承诺安全的解决方案，防腐剂和添加剂充斥着食品供应：止咳糖浆中的吗啡、牛奶中的白垩、肉类中的甲醛。 政府化学家哈维·华盛顿·威利（Harvey Washington Wiley）认识到这些未经证实的创新对公共健康构成了威胁。 为了证明这一点，威利招募了一批年轻人，他们愿意吃含有这些防腐剂的食物，同时科学家观察其影响。 这支所谓的“毒药小队”的苦难促成了 1906 年《纯净食品和药品法案》的出台。

摘自1909年2月号：城市工人的食物

我们正处于现代 Wiley 时刻。 人工智能的创新正在为当今的家庭带来非常实实在在的好处：比人类筛查人员更早发现发育迟缓的诊断辅助工具、允许非英语移民父母与孩子的老师互动的实时翻译工具、减轻许多父母和教育工作者的行政负担的生产力应用程序。 但这些创新也带来了明显的危险：泰迪熊会描述性怪癖或教幼儿点燃火柴，人工智能生成的视频会突出显示虚构的字母和单词。

尽管存在这些人工智能出错的戏剧性例子，但真正的危险（正如我们的食物供应所证明的那样）是当这些系统完全按照设计运行时会发生什么。

到了 20 世纪中叶，食品公司发现了比养活人们更有利可图的东西：激发人们继续吃东西的欲望。 他们聘请了科学家——化学家、风味工程师、行为研究人员——来寻找精确的配方，以超越身体发出的“够了”的自然信号。 他们发现了“幸福点”——糖、脂肪和盐的精确组合，可以最大限度地提高人脑的愉悦感——并设计了食物来达到这一目标。 他们开始生产现在所谓的超加工食品。

这种新食物看起来就像它更天然的前身。 它以熟悉的形状出现。 它位于同一个架子上。 但一些根本性的事情发生了变化。 尽管对于哪些食品属于广义的超加工食品存在一些模糊性和争议——在某些方面，这是“垃圾食品”的一种奇特说法——但其中许多食品都含有添加剂，并且经过精心设计，易于大量食用和消化。 他们可能会使用经过精心设计的超美味组合来点亮我们大脑的奖励系统。 天然食品如何与之竞争？

简而言之：他们不能。 全食慢慢从我们的饮食中消失。 如今，美国人平均每天摄入的热量有 55% 来自超加工食品，而这些食品在一个世纪前甚至还不存在。 对于 1 至 18 岁的儿童，这一数字接近 62%。 根据 CDC 的国家健康和营养检查调查，从 2001 年到 2018 年，成年人从天然食品中消耗的热量从 32.7% 下降到 27.4%。 根据 2021 年 CDC 的分析，近三分之一的 1 至 5 岁美国儿童每天不吃水果，近一半的儿童每天不吃蔬菜。 超过一半的人每周喝含糖饮料。

食品公司开发出真正卓越的创新来解决非常现实的挑战。 但有了这些创新，他们也开始增加收入。 同样的市场逻辑现在也被应用到我们与科技的互动中。 人工智能的基本功能非常出色，但也可以对其进行优化以提高参与度。

乍一看，与人工智能同伴交谈的孩子就像是在参与对话。 但重要的、安静的互动已被剥夺。 不完美、拖延以及道歉或改写某些事情的需要似乎是人类沟通中的缺陷，但事实上，它们是至关重要的发展基石。 误解之后发生的破裂和修复的小循环在童年时期上演了数千次，这就是韧性、灵活性和情绪调节能力的建立过程。 这就是孩子们发展最重要的人际关系技能的方式：相信人际关系能够在冲突中幸存下来，并在不适时与他人保持联系。

摘自2025年12月号：反社交媒体时代已经到来

如果消除童年时期的摩擦，社交情感系统就永远得不到正常发展所需的东西。 本应通过不完美、有时令人沮丧的人类互动构建的神经结构可能永远不会完全形成。 挫折容忍度、同理心或复原力也不会。 认知技能也可能受到影响。 发展科学家很早就认识到，孩子们通过遇到超出其当前能力的任务来学习和成长。 这被称为“最近发展区”，人工智能系统旨在准确地满足孩子所处的风险，从而剥夺他们到达该区域的机会。

因为人工智能伴侣的设计目的是消除每一个缺陷——误解、延迟、修复——孩子的社交情感系统永远不需要工作。 超加工食品会剥夺饮食中的纤维，而参与度优化的人工智能可能会消除童年时期的摩擦。 正在发育的心智就像肠道一样，需要抵抗力才能生长。 摩擦并不是发展的障碍，而是发展的障碍。这是发展。

并非每个人都会同样受到这项新技术的推出的影响。 粮食安全水平非常低的人比粮食安全水平高的人消耗的超加工食品大约多 3%，部分原因是每卡路里未加工食品的成本是超加工食品的 2.5 倍以上。 然而，一旦超加工食品的潜在危害变得明显，高收入家庭就开始远离此类食品。 对于那些拥有资源的人来说，“清洁”原料、最低限度加工的食品和有机农产品变得可用且负担得起。 “有机”饮食成为身份的象征。

阅读：最好的养育秘诀就是变得富有

人工智能也出现了同样的模式。 许多开发这些产品的工程师和管理人员都在家中远离屏幕，并加倍进行非结构化游戏。 Anthropic 的联合创始人 Jack Clark 今年早些时候告诉 Ezra Klein，他的小女儿能够“不受限制地”访问 YouTube 算法的想法“让我感到害怕”。 他补充道，“我有典型的加州技术高管的观点，即没有那么多适合儿童的技术。”

如果食品类比成立，那么参与度优化的人工智能将成为新的美元菜单，专注于最无力承担其发展成本的儿童的生活。 皮尤研究中心已经通过调查数据证明，与高收入家庭的青少年相比，低收入家庭的青少年更有可能依赖聊天机器人完成家庭作业。

我们还没有对在超处理互动中长大的儿童进行大规模研究。 这项研究还需要几十年的时间。 但让我彻夜难眠的是，我们有可能让人际关系成为新的有机体——受到富人的珍惜和保护，而其他人却无法接触到。
